title: Asserting Collaborator Output (Assertion Duplication)
pattern: A test that makes assertions about the specific formatting or output characteristics of an injected collaborator's return values instead of validating only the test subject's own logic.
why_bad: It duplicates tests and raises suite maintenance costs [111]. The responsibility for asserting a method's return value lies strictly with its receiver [111]. Checking it elsewhere couples the caller's test to the collaborator's data schemas [111].
detection: The assertions in class A's test file verify exact properties of data generated by class B, rather than checking how A transforms or utilizes that data.
counterexample: Using a state check on A's own public fields to verify that A correctly routed or processed the generic collaborator output.
fix: Restrict the test to verifying that the subject sends the correct message (using a mock) or focus assertions strictly on the subject's own business conversions [111, 113].
